dedupe_keys.name: fused twin base bim derived building model with 390 indoor lorawan sensor locations unity project

description: Fused Twin Base is a Unity project containing a building model derived from a BIM model and exported to FBX, with the positions of 390 indoor sensors and 4 gateways shown at their real locations in the physical building. It was released on Zenodo on 11 March 2022 (version 1.0.0) by Jascha Grübel and Michal Gath-Morad of ETH Zürich, as a stand-alone version of the DAVE visualisation of sensor locations. The sensor IDs map to device IDs in a separate Zenodo dataset of LoRaWAN transmission metadata, and the spatial layout was used to derive walls and distances between sensors and gateways in studies of passively sensing human presence with dense indoor LoRaWAN networks and of Fused Twins, which show a digital twin in place in its physical twin. Coverage: one instrumented building; the ETH location is inferred from the authors' affiliation, as the building is not named in the README. Access: repository and Zenodo archive of about 9 MB. Licence: GNU AGPL version 3 per Zenodo; free. Caveats: a visualisation project, not a full BIM model. Simulation uses: indoor digital twin prototyping and sensor network analysis. Related records: the BIM4EEB sensor measurements and the D2EPC smart house.
